question: Does a common signed causal calibration of point-force two-end transport trained at beta=.2001 improve whole-stroke measured-nut AC reconstruction at beta=.1886 versus retaining source geometry, causal empirical FIRs and signed/scale-fit half-period shift?
membership: 1–50 source, every fifth solely for hyperparameter selection, remaining40 solely fit. Entire held strokes51–56 (one next position, same specimen/day/robot folder); no trimming of full metric, equal per-stroke weights. No claimed force assignment.
input: Only bridge in held forecast and independently recorded beta. Held bow speed selects the registered secondary onset and is otherwise unused. Nut omitted by numeric usecols in held predictor. All mixed-channel raw bytes hashed/CRC verified. Both endpoints identical fourth-order 25–800Hz causal Butterworth bandpass applied at acquiring 50kHz, subtract first same-channel sample for fixed cold baseline, score every 10th sample. A complete 5.16s first training stroke is observed. The 100ms onset window begins at the first 10 ms sustained |measured speed|>=.02 m/s.
mechanism: x_nut/x_bridge=sinh(k a)/sinh(k(L-a)) with one-way attenuation rho and propagation delay τ=L/c, no free bow-friction fit. Echo series built through whole finite course, linear interpolation at50kHz then causal filtering. rho=.65,.85,.95,.985 and f0=93,98,103 Hz; source validation across10 untouched-source strokes chooses f0,loss and regression regularization for each family. Fitted signed 31-tap FIR calibrates sensor/support phase; physical gain-only control retained. Direct causal 81/241-tap FIR and signed/scaled half-period shift tuned on same train/dev data. Separate identical calibration with geometry held at source median isolates position conditioning. The inverse is not bounded near the bridge antiresonance and measured supports/sensors and distributed bow compete with this model.
endpoints: Seven float32 forecast arrays for each held stroke are whole-byte pinned before scoring; score receiver requires exact SHA/census including unchanged source member identity. Primary mean per-stroke RMSE(N) must beat source geometry, both learned FIRs and signed shift; at least4/6 complete-stroke wins against each, and >=4/6 onset-window wins against better source-dev FIR. Report whole, pre-motion and onset RMSE/MAE/max on all42 arrays and all worst raw windows. No score-dependent gain, polarity, phase shift, lag, clipping or exclusions. No claim that the source f0 sweep estimates a physical string property.
